title: Continuous cellular automata show the same four classes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Continuous cellular automata show the same four classes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cellular automata whose cells take continuous gray-level values show essentially the same four classes of behavior as discrete cellular automata, with class 4 behavior and its discrete localized structures typically appearing at transitions as the rule parameter is varied.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But it seems that this behavior falls into essentially the same four classes that we have already seen in ordinary cellular automata.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Four Classes of Behavior” (from p. 231), p. 242. Scope: continuous cellular automata with a smoothly varying rule parameter

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The cited families can be simulated now, yielding a meaningful restricted test. Available coverage is not representative of continuous cellular automata in general, and the taxonomy remains interpretive.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sweep the parameter of specified continuous-valued cellular automata from random starts, classify runs by explicit order, entropy, and localized-structure metrics, and test whether four clusters recur and class 4-like structures concentrate near transitions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Existing catalogs cover few continuous rule families.

Four-class mapping is not uniquely operationalized.

Discretization and numerical precision can change outcomes.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The continuous family is an explicit formula, so a parameter scan is ordinary numerical work and can be finished quickly. Calling the output essentially the same four classes adds an interpretation step that discrete rules do not need, and localized structures have to be separated from display choices. The scan tests this family well and the broader wording only through that proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Scan the averaging-plus-fractional-part family as the additive constant runs from 0 to 1, and tag each value by activity and by whether discrete localized structures appear. Four regimes in the same order as discrete classes, with localized structures at the transitions, would support the claim for this family.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Localized structures can depend on how the gray levels are displayed.

The evidence is one parametrized family, while continuous cellular automata are a wider class.

Gray-level pictures still need a mapping onto the four discrete classes.

analysis feasibility: 0.8
